record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: If the exponential Toda interaction e^x is replaced by a general force law F(x) that is a sufficiently small perturbation of e^x and admits a suitable 2-periodic solution, does the corresponding shock problem still have the same long-time asymptotic behavior as the Toda shock problem, and how can that behavior be analyzed rigorously?

evidence.quote: Second open problem: Analyze the general shock problem (15) for suitably small perturbations F(x) of ex.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a one-dimensional infinite chain of unit-mass particles with positions $q_n(t)$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, governed by the Newtonian equations of motion
$$\ddot q_n(t)=F\bigl(q_{n+1}(t)-q_n(t)\bigr)-F\bigl(q_n(t)-q_{n-1}(t)\bigr),\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z},\ t>0,$$
with shock-type initial data consisting of two semi-infinite lattices in equilibrium, moving toward each other so that asymptotically as $n\to -\infty$ the particles travel with velocity $2c>0$ and as $n\to +\infty$ with velocity $0$ (or equivalent step-like Flaschka variables for the relative displacements). 

The classical Toda case corresponds to the exponential force law $F(x)=e^x$, in which case the system is completely integrable and the long-time behavior of $q_{n+1}(t)-q_n(t)$ and $\dot q_n(t)$ is known: for $n/t$ in a finite interval the lattice converges to a modulated $2$-periodic (genus-one) finite-gap Toda solution, while outside this interval it converges to the two constant equilibria; the modulation parameters and the wedge of oscillation are explicitly computable from the integrable structure.

Now suppose $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth function that is a sufficiently small perturbation of $e^x$ (in a suitable norm) and that the perturbed lattice still admits a $2$-periodic traveling-wave solution analogous to the Toda $2$-periodic solution used in the integrable analysis. 

Prove or disprove: the corresponding shock problem for the perturbed force law $F$ exhibits the same long-time asymptotic behavior as the Toda shock problem, namely convergence (in an appropriate sense, locally uniformly on rays $n/t=\xi$) to the two constant states outside a wedge and to a modulated $2$-periodic profile inside the wedge, with the wedge boundaries and the modulation determined by the perturbed $2$-periodic solution. Provide a rigorous analytic framework (necessarily non-integrable, since $F\ne e^x$) for establishing this asymptotic description.
artifact.category_tag: Toda shock and nonintegrable lattice perturbations
artifact.status_search_result: Recent rigorous results (e.g., Egorova–Michor–Teschl and collaborators, 2020s) have justified the long-time asymptotics of the integrable Toda shock problem via nonlinear steepest descent, confirming the Venakides–Deift–Oba conjecture in the exponential case. However, no published work appears to extend this asymptotic analysis to general non-integrable small perturbations $F(x)$ of $e^x$, which would require non-integrable techniques. The problem of analyzing the shock problem for perturbed force laws thus appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Long-Time Asymptotics for the Toda Shock Problem: Non-Overlapping Spectra
status_evidence.snippet: Long-time asymptotics for the Toda shock problem derived via nonlinear steepest descent; verifies the Venakides–Deift–Oba conjecture in the exponential (integrable) case.
status_evidence.claim: The integrable Toda shock case has been rigorously analyzed, but only for the exponential force law.

status_evidence.title: Toda shock waves: justification of asymptotics
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous justification of the asymptotic behavior of the Toda shock waves using Riemann-Hilbert methods.
status_evidence.claim: Justification exists for the Toda (exponential) case; perturbed (non-integrable) force laws are not addressed.
